drug_class: Serotonin reuptake inhibitor and partial serotonin receptor agonist (SPARI)
purpose: Vilazodone is used to treat depression in adults. It helps improve your mood, sleep, appetite, and energy levels. It can also help restore your interest in daily activities and reduce feelings of anxiety that often come along with depression.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called serotonin to help regulate your mood. Vilazodone works in two ways — it helps keep more serotonin available in your brain, and it also gently activates certain serotonin receptors directly. Think of it like both keeping the fuel in the tank longer and also giving the engine a small extra boost at the same time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and dizziness, especially when you first start taking it. You might also notice trouble sleeping, dry mouth, or feeling unusually tired. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Do not take vilazodone if you are taking or have recently taken a medication called an MAO inhibitor — this combination can be very dangerous. Like other antidepressants, it may increase thoughts of suicide in some people, especially young adults under 25, so it is important to report any unusual mood changes to your doctor right away. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: You usually start with 10 mg once a day with food for the first week, then increase to 20 mg once a day for the next week, and then your doctor may raise it to 40 mg once a day. Always take it with a meal to help your body absorb it properly and to reduce stomach side effects.
